title: The Last Thorn Anew
premise: Ines Galloway has survived twelve years in the city of Vellamarch by hiding her gift for speaking with beasts, selling charms that are mostly harmless trickery. When the crown's new Witch-Hunters burn the market quarter and a dying wolf entrusts her with the location of the Thornheart—the seed of the old wild magic the kingdom thought destroyed—Ines learns the hunt is not random: the queen is hunting the seed to devour its power and rule unchallenged. Pursued by Hunter-Captain Rell, who once was her friend, Ines must carry the Thornheart to the ruined grove beyond the mountains and plant it before the solstice. She succeeds only by giving up her own gift to feed the seed, ending her magic but reigniting the old wild law—and Rell, changed by what she witnesses, lets her walk away and begins quietly dismantling the hunt from within.
about_author: Silas Yarrow is the pen name of a former field botanist who spent a decade cataloguing hedgerows and listening, as they claim, to more than the wind. They write fantasy about people who keep small secrets in large, unforgiving cities.

chapters.title: Charms and Cinders
chapters.summary: In Ines's POV, we see her careful double life: selling charms, trading quiet words with the market's rats and pigeons, and dodging the attention of Hunter-Captain Rell, who inspects her stall with an old familiarity. When Witch-Hunters torch the market quarter and a mortally wounded wolf staggers into her cellar, Ines's instinct to help overrides her caution. The wolf presses a burning seed—the Thornheart—into her hands and dies speaking her name. The emotional beat is dread: invisibility has just become impossible.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Still Ines's POV, she flees the city with Rell's hunt close behind, guided by the Thornheart's pull toward the mountain grove. Along the road she encounters beasts who remember the old war and test her worthiness, forcing her to admit the gift she's spent twelve years denying. A confrontation with Rell at a river crossing reveals the captain suspects her but hesitates to name her. The beat is reluctant acceptance: Ines stops running from what she is and starts running toward what she must do.

chapters.title: The Queen's Hungry Garden
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Rell, who reports to Queen Sabrah and glimpses the truth: the queen's private garden holds the withered husks of every magical thing the hunt has seized, and the Thornheart is the last living seed she needs to become something more than mortal. Ordered to bring Ines alive, Rell realizes she is complicit in devouring the world's wild law. She chooses deception, feeding the queen false routes. The beat is moral rupture—Rell's loyalty to the crown breaks against her memory of who Ines once was.

chapters.title: The Last Thorn
chapters.summary: Ines reaches the ruined grove on solstice eve with Rell's hunters minutes behind, and discovers the seed will only take root if fed a willing gift. She pours her beast-speech into the earth, losing her magic forever as the grove erupts green and the old wild law floods back across the land, stripping the queen's stolen power. Rell arrives to find Ines powerless and lets her go. In the quiet aftermath, Ines plants an ordinary garden, deaf now to beasts but finally at peace. The beat is costly, earned renewal.
